doc.title: Emile Christian and Anthony Sbarbaro Interview, 1959-02-11

title: Picnics, beer, prices, Spanish Fort and Millenburg
summary: Picnic pay and prices, Lake Pontchartrain resorts and regret over the lost Millenburg.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: as much as anyone. Well during that time everything was so cheap you know. Look when we used to go out to lake and play those picnics. Three o'clock. Nine o'clock in the morning till six o'clock in the evening.
Well you had your fun too. Yeah you had a lot of fun. If you had more fun those days what you're having now. Today it's money
and it's hard work. People used to pay a dollar and a half a couple to come in place. A dollar and a half a couple.
For a picnic was that? Yeah a dollar and a half a couple. But I think if they fed them they had to pay three dollars.

Yeah all those things you see. In those picnics out there they run out of beer. They'd go right down the end of the wharf. Buy a quarter barrel of beer. A dollar and sixty five cents. A dollar sixty five cents. And they'd roll it up.
I had beer. Beer all day long. Beer all day long. It was a pleasure to play a fan. You're dancing. You're eating. And your women out there too huh? Yeah women was galore.
Well I mean people used to go out there but on Sunday they'd all be dressed up in their whites.

I think New Orleans missed the boat when they did away with Mount Lomborgon. And I mean the train used to be damp. They should have kept it and beautified it. I mean. You know really make it pretty because that that is the background of New Orleans. That was something. Well what was Spanish Fort like? Well Spanish Fort wasn't nothing like it. Not like it is right. It used to be Millenburg. They tried to make a small Coney Island out of it but they were never successful. That and West End. Look what West End looks like today. There's another place they're missing a boat. Brutal. No nothing was like Millenburg. Millenburg was really something. Yeah we should have seen the night ridges. Yeah that was pictures. Well it's something like this. For instance New York nightlife. Why is it New York nightlife when we opened there in 1917 that they had three rooms. Each with a seating capacity for about 600. and a little better. Three floors running every night in a week. Each one of them had something different. That's why they brought us in there. The second floor was a fizzle. They took us in this room. What the hell are they going to lose?
